subject: Recap: Deployment options & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Deployment options & next steps (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Hi Alicia, thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

What I heard
- Primary goal: serve customer-facing analytics features with strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Key drivers: compliance (data separation), predictable latency for user requests, and internal security review prefers no public internet egress.

Deployment options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to prod, lower operational overhead, but data goes through Redwood-hosted endpoints (not preferred for this use case).
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; data isolation within our infra might address some requirements but still goes over Redwood-managed network.
- Private VPC (recommended for Acme): customer-controlled network (VPC peering or PrivateLink) or on-prem package for air-gapped environments. This gives you control over routing, IP allowlists, and KMS integration.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm you want to pursue Private VPC (peering or PrivateLink)? If so we'll schedule a 30-min network call with our solutions engineer (Marissa) and your infra lead to agree on the pattern.
2) Please share: preferred contact for networking (name/email), whether you prefer VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink, and any constraints on IP ranges or transit gateways.
3) I've attached a short checklist and a network diagram stub, Marissa will walk through these on the call.

Attachments: network_diagram.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-checklist.xlsx

Thanks, available for a quick call early next week.

Sean Gallagher

Thanks Sean, good summary. We are strongly leaning toward Private VPC due to our compliance needs. A few clarifying questions before we set the infra call: 

- For PrivateLink vs VPC peering: which option gives us the simplest flow for audit logs and avoids changes to our existing route tables? Our infra team prefers minimal routing changes.
- Do you provide sample IP allowlist ranges for outbound connections from our side, or is it purely an inbound peering setup?
- Timeline: once we agree on the pattern, how long is a typical setup (engineering + network approvals)? We have a security review on July 8th and would like something in place before then if possible.

Thanks Alicia, great questions. Short answers below, happy to go into detail on the call.

On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 8:45 PM Alicia Moreno <alicia.moreno@acmeanalytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sean, good summary. We are strongly leaning toward Private VPC due to our compliance needs. A few clarifying questions before we set the infra call: 
> 
> - For PrivateLink vs VPC peering: which option gives us the simplest flow for audit logs and avoids changes to our existing route tables? Our infra team prefers minimal routing changes.
> - Do you provide sample IP allowlist ranges for outbound connections from our side, or is it purely an inbound peering setup?
> - Timeline: once we agree on the pattern, how long is a typical setup (engineering + network approvals)? We have a security review on July 8th and would like something in place before then if possible.
>
Answers: 
- PrivateLink (AWS) is typically the lighter-weight option from a routing perspective; it presents an interface endpoint in your VPC so you don't need to modify route tables. It's also easier to restrict at the subnet/security group level which helps with audit/logging.
- VPC peering gives lower latency and direct L3 routing; it's a good fit if you need high throughput and want native routing between VPCs. It may require route table updates and coordination with your network team.
- For IP allowlists: if you use PrivateLink we can provide the interface endpoint DNS name (no IPs to manage). For peering we provide the peer VPC CIDR and the subset of IPs we expect to originate egress (we'll provide a recommended small set of NAT egress ranges).
- Timeline: typical PrivateLink setup with our checklist and support is about 3-7 business days once both teams approve network access and we receive the required VPC IDs and contact. Peering can be similar but sometimes slower if your security team requires additional review.

Proposed next step: schedule a 30-min call this week with your infra lead and Marissa (our solutions engineer) to pick PrivateLink vs peering and capture the exact artifacts we need. Marissa, can you take the lead on the invite and walk through the attached checklist?

Sean
